harness_note: Codex CLI connects through `trialm bridge`, which passes its requests to Ollama's Chat Completions API at http://127.0.0.1:11434 as model qwen3.6:35b-a3b-trialm.

steps.title: Check what is already installed
steps.why: triaLM did not find Ollama. These read-only commands confirm what is installed and running, and that there is room for the 22.1 GB download. A failing version command means the runtime is not installed or not on PATH.

steps.title: Install Ollama
steps.why: Official install script: installs /usr/local/bin/ollama (with CUDA/ROCm libraries when it finds a GPU) and an `ollama` systemd service that starts the server on port 11434. It uses sudo.

steps.title: Download Qwen3.6 35B-A3B Q4_K_M (22.1 GB)
steps.why: Pulls the exact Q4_K_M GGUF from Hugging Face (unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF) — the file triaLM's prediction is based on. If Ollama reports an unsupported architecture for this file, use the library build instead: `ollama pull qwen3.6:35b-a3b`.

steps.title: Create qwen3.6:35b-a3b-trialm with a 65536-token context
steps.why: Ollama's default context depends on GPU memory (often 4096 tokens) and the OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs cannot change it per request; a Modelfile with num_ctx fixes it for this model only. The new model shares the downloaded weights (no extra disk). Use qwen3.6:35b-a3b-trialm as the model name in your harness.

files.content:
# Generated by trialm plan: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B Q4_K_M on Ollama.
FROM hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_M
PARAMETER num_ctx 65536

steps.title: Set Ollama server settings: OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1
steps.why: Server-wide settings for never unload the model when idle (default: 5 minutes, after which the next request reloads it and re-processes the whole prompt). Ollama reads them only from the server's environment at start-up, so they are set persistently and the server is restarted. Running models are unloaded by the restart. This writes a systemd drop-in (same effect as `sudo systemctl edit ollama`) for the service the install script created. If you run `ollama serve` yourself, export the variables in that shell instead.

steps.title: Load qwen3.6:35b-a3b-trialm and check GPU placement
steps.why: Preloads the model so the first harness request does not pay the load time. In `ollama ps`, CONTEXT should read 65536 and PROCESSOR should read 100% GPU (anything else means part of the model runs on the CPU and will be much slower than predicted).

steps.title: Start the Codex CLI bridge
steps.why: Codex sends requests that local runtimes' own Responses endpoints do not fully handle (namespaced tools, several developer messages, hosted web search; llama.cpp skips namespace tools and strict chat templates reject a second system message). `trialm bridge` accepts Codex CLI's requests on port 11535 (or the next free port) and passes them to http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions, the runtime's most mature API, with system messages merged for the model's chat template and tool calls mapped back; runtime errors are shown in Codex CLI instead of being retried. It returns once it answers and prints the exact Codex CLI command.

steps.title: Start Codex CLI with qwen3.6:35b-a3b-trialm
steps.why: Everything is passed with -c overrides, so no Codex config file is edited, plain `codex` keeps working as before, and nothing depends on Codex's config layout (profiles moved to separate files in 0.134). Use the command the bridge printed: it has the real port and, when codex is not on your terminal's PATH, its full path. Web search is off because a local model cannot run OpenAI's hosted search.

commands.run: codex -c model_providers.trialm.name=trialm -c model_providers.trialm.base_url=http://127.0.0.1:11535/v1 -c model_providers.trialm.wire_api=responses -c model_provider=trialm -c web_search=disabled -c model_context_window=65536 -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=52428 -m qwen3.6:35b-a3b-trialm

steps.restart: Codex CLI: start a new session in your own terminal

steps.title: Verify the setup
steps.why: Checks that Ollama answers at http://127.0.0.1:11434 with qwen3.6:35b-a3b-trialm, that the context window is 65536 tokens and compares real speed with triaLM's prediction. It then sends requests in codex's own format (a greeting, a tool call and the tool result) and reports "Ready" only if all three work: a fast runtime can still reject a coding tool's requests. The setup is not done until this says Ready.

commands.run: trialm verify --runtime ollama --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:11434 --model qwen3.6:35b-a3b-trialm --catalog-model qwen3.6-35b-a3b --quant Q4_K_M --ctx 65536 --harness codex

warnings: Restarting the Ollama service unloads any running models.
These steps need administrator rights (sudo): Install Ollama; Set Ollama server settings: OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1.
The model download is 22.1 GB; keep at least 26.3 GB of disk space free.
